purpose: Four independent PNG frames; not integrated until full cycle review

prompts.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: ONE transparent PNG frame for a 2D pixel-art game run cycle. Produce exactly one character in exactly one pose, no sheet, no grid, no variants, no text.
Input image: identity and style reference of the approved female game character, not a background.
Create frame 01 of a four-frame RUN RIGHT cycle. Right-facing profile, identical brown long wavy hair, face, large head, dark grey jacket, light grey shirt, black trousers, dark shoes. Female figure has a slightly shorter stature and narrower waist than the male characters. Keep the reference's compact pixel-art proportions and crisp square pixel blocks, limited stable palette, no soft shading or anti-aliased painted details.
Canvas 1280 x 1280 with genuine transparent alpha. Character should occupy the same proportions as the reference 256 square enlarged exactly 5 times: head top around y260, hair/body center x640, feet baseline y1120; entire character stays within x330..970. Keep head and torso perfectly vertical, right-facing, fixed in place for later frames, no tilt or head bob.
RUN POSE phase 01, first contact: the NEAR leg (character's right leg, the large visible foreground leg) reaches FORWARD toward screen RIGHT, the FAR leg extends BACK toward screen LEFT. The NEAR arm, the larger sleeve on the viewer-facing side, swings BACK toward screen LEFT with hand clearly to the LEFT of the waist. The FAR arm swings FORWARD toward screen RIGHT. Opposed arm/leg swing, readable separate legs. Both feet near the same baseline. This is running, not a standing pose.
Lock identity and preserve all hairstyle, facial, clothing and palette details. Only limb pose changes. No weapon, hat, accessories, outline glow, cast shadow, floor or scenery. Do not mirror the character or turn the head.

Use case: identity-preserve. Asset: ONE separate transparent pixel-art PNG animation frame, never a spritesheet.
The supplied image is the exact female character model and exact composition to preserve. Make only ONE animation edit: limb positions for frame 02, the passing phase between the first and opposite run contacts, running toward SCREEN RIGHT.
Keep the supplied canvas size 1254 x 1254, transparent background, same pixel block size, same scale, head top/eyes/hair outline in exactly the same coordinates, same face, same brown hair, same dark grey jacket and light grey shirt, same narrow waist and black trousers/shoes, same torso coordinates. Head and torso must not bob, rotate, shrink or stretch. Retain all original palette and shading.
Limb pose ONLY: the NEAR/right leg (foreground leg) now points DOWN almost under the hip, with the near shoe at ground baseline y1115. The FAR/left leg is lifted and bent FORWARD toward screen RIGHT: its knee is ahead of the hip and its foot tucked back below the knee; this far leg must be clearly lifted off the ground. The two shoes should not overlap. Arms pass near the sides of the waist, near/foreground arm bent with hand slightly behind the waist toward screen LEFT, far arm slightly forward toward screen RIGHT; hands remain visibly separate.
Do NOT reuse the wide split-leg contact pose in the reference. This is the narrower passing pose of the same run, not a different character. Do NOT mirror the whole image or the head. Exactly one character, no text, no marks, no scenery, no shadow. Preserve genuine transparent alpha.

Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: exactly ONE transparent pixel-art PNG animation frame, not a sheet.
Input is frame 01 of the same female RUN RIGHT animation. Preserve this exact woman and all coordinates of her hair, face and torso. Produce frame 03: OPPOSITE CONTACT, half a run cycle later.
Keep the original square canvas 1254 x 1254 and original transparent alpha, exact pixel block size, limited palette and outline. Same brown long wavy hair and big head, same face looking SCREEN RIGHT, same dark grey jacket/light shirt, same narrow waist, black trousers, dark shoes. Head top around y278, same head/torso/hip coordinates and size as input, ground baseline around y1115. No head bob, body tilt, scaling or changing clothing.
CRITICAL REQUIRED CHANGE, arms: the LARGE VISIBLE NEAR ARM must now swing FORWARD toward SCREEN RIGHT, bent at the elbow, with the foreground sleeve and hand visibly IN FRONT OF THE CHEST on the screen-right side. This is the opposite of the input, whose big near arm points backwards. The FAR arm now swings backwards toward screen LEFT, with the small far hand visible behind the waist.
CRITICAL REQUIRED CHANGE, legs: the LARGE VISIBLE NEAR LEG now extends BACK toward SCREEN LEFT and its shoe is to the LEFT of the hip. The FAR LEG extends FORWARD toward SCREEN RIGHT and its shoe is to the RIGHT of the hip. Maintain correct near-leg foreground overlap at the hip. The near arm and near leg move in opposite directions. This must be a genuinely new opposite-contact pose, not the input contact repeated.
Change ONLY arm/leg positions. Do not mirror the whole character, head, face, jacket fasteners or hair. Exactly one figure; no grid, text, marks, scene, shadow, floor or extra items. Genuine transparent background.

Use case: identity-preserve. Asset: exactly ONE separate PNG frame on transparent background for a right-facing pixel-art woman run cycle. No sprite sheet.
The reference is frame 01 and is the immutable character model. Produce frame 04, the SECOND PASSING PHASE, after opposite contact. Preserve every head, hairstyle, face and torso pixel position, size, palette and clothing detail. Same 1254 x 1254 canvas, pixel block size and alpha. Same long brown wavy hair, right-facing big head, dark grey jacket, light grey inner shirt, narrow waist, black pants, dark shoes. Keep head top around y278 and torso/hip placement fixed. No bobbing, rotation, shrinking, stretching or palette drift.
Required NEW limb pose: the FAR/left leg supports the body, extending DOWN almost vertically with its shoe on baseline y1115, slightly behind/left of hip. The NEAR/right leg is lifted and bent FORWARD toward SCREEN RIGHT; this near knee must visibly overlap in FRONT of the hip/other leg and its foreground shoe must be raised off the ground toward screen RIGHT, tucked beneath the knee. Clearly separate shoes, one grounded and one raised. This is the opposite passing phase from the first passing frame: now the foreground/near leg is the lifted bent leg and the rear/far leg is the vertical supporting leg.
Arms: NEAR arm is returning from forward swing, bent and close to chest on SCREEN RIGHT; its larger foreground sleeve crosses the side/front of the torso and hand points slightly right. FAR arm is returning from back swing, its smaller hand slightly behind the waist toward SCREEN LEFT. Preserve opposite arm/leg motion; no stretched limbs.
Change ONLY limbs. Do not repeat wide split-leg contact. Do not mirror head, hair or entire character. One character only, no floor, cast shadow, scene, labels, grid or marks. Genuine alpha transparency.
